Здравствуйте!

Спасибо, Надежда, за ответ и шаблон NDA. В нём необходимо предусмотреть обе раскрывающие стороны: меня лично и PBK. Просим уточнить, для чего на этапе NDA требуются СНИЛС и ИНН и можно ли согласовать NDA по минимально необходимым идентификационным данным; необходимые документы предоставим согласованным безопасным способом.

Просим оценить подготовку и подачу российских патентных заявок на основании всего портфеля PPA №1–10. Приоритетные технические группы: №1 — Modular Cabinet Platform (PPA №3–7), №2 — AI Pricing & Retail Intelligence Platform (PPA №1,2,8,9); PPA №10 — отдельная группа учёта тары в торговой зоне. Обозначения NPPA №1 и №2 используются здесь только для сопоставления материалов с американским проектом; российские заявки необходимо подготовить по требованиям России. Количество и группировку российских заявок просим предложить после анализа. Подачу в США будем поручать американскому поверенному. Дополнительно просим сообщить, сможете ли вы законно представлять заявителя при подготовке и подаче соответствующих PCT. Исполнитель PCT будет выбран отдельно из российских или американских кандидатов после проверки полномочий; это не поручение на подачу. Передача прав PBK → Михаил Козин требует проверки; её завершение не предполагается.

По нашему реестру, который просим сверить с официальными квитанциями: PPA №1 — 63/938,244 от 11 декабря 2025; №2 — 63/945,513 от 19 декабря 2025; №8 — 64/090,283 от 14 июня 2026; №9 — 64/106,825 от 7 июля 2026. Самая ранняя дата группы NPPA №1: PPA №3 — 63/947,909 от 23 декабря 2025. Рабочие контрольные даты — 11 декабря 2026 для группы №2 и 23 декабря 2026 для группы №1; просим подтвердить применимые сроки и приоритетную поддержку. Я гражданин России, проживаю в Sharjah, ОАЭ, по-английски не говорю; предпочитаю письменную переписку с возможностью перевода.

Чтобы не повторять уже обсуждённое, по известным пунктам достаточно подтвердить прежний ответ; по остальным просим коротко ответить с сохранением нумерации.

1. Объём: готовы ли вы подготовить и подать российские заявки по PPA №1–10, начиная с групп №1 и №2? Какие услуги по PCT вы могли бы выполнить при наличии необходимых полномочий? Подача в США в ваш объём не включается.

2. Команда: кто будет основным исполнителем и кто лично проведёт окончательную проверку описания, формулы, приоритетов и документов на подачу? Укажите профессиональный статус и регистрационный номер.

3. PCT: сможете ли вы организовать представительство с учётом российского гражданства и проживания заявителя в Sharjah, ОАЭ? Кто именно вправе представлять заявителя перед выбранным получающим ведомством, в том числе RO/IB, и на каком основании? Если нужен партнёр, укажите его роль и стоимость либо порядок её согласования.

4. Приоритеты: сможете ли вы проверить квитанции, раскрытие PPA №1–10 и цепочку прав, подтвердить применимые сроки и основания приоритета российских заявок и отдельно возможных PCT? Просим прежде всего проверить группы №1 и №2.

5. График: когда вы сможете начать, представить первые проекты, завершить проверку и подать документы по каждой группе? Просим учесть наиболее раннюю дату группы NPPA №2 и назвать резерв времени и зависимости от нас.

6. Материалы: сможете ли вы принять незавершённую работу Ali по NPPA №1 и использовать пригодные описания и рисунки? По NPPA №2 просим оценить подготовку на основании PPA №1,2,8,9; наличие готового проекта NPPA №2 не предполагается. Что необходимо для оценки и какие переделки оплачиваются отдельно?

7. Конфиденциальность: готовы ли вы подписать NDA с двумя раскрывающими сторонами — Михаилом Козиным лично и PBK ENGINEERING INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS MANAGEMENT - FZCO? Если нужны изменения, предложите их. Полный технический пакет передадим после согласования и подписания NDA; при невозможности подписать просим прямо сообщить.

8. Страхование и рекомендации: есть ли страхование профессиональной ответственности? По возможности и с согласия клиентов будем благодарны за одну-две рекомендации. Если эти сведения нельзя предоставить, достаточно это указать.

9. Стоимость: просим отдельно оценить российские заявки по группам №1, №2 и PPA №10, а также каждый возможный PCT как отдельную опцию. Отделите гонорары, пошлины, поиск, переводы, рисунки, налоги и услуги партнёров; укажите валюту, аванс, этапы оплаты, исключения и предварительный общий бюджет по России. Американские услуги не включайте. Если нужна оценка материалов, укажите диапазон и условия уточнения.

10. Следующий шаг: какие условия договора, документы и действия нужны для начала? Можно ли сначала бесплатно оценить объём после NDA; если нужна платная проверка, просим предварительно согласовать её объём и стоимость. Этот запрос и передача материалов не являются принятием предложения или разрешением на платную работу/подачу.

Мы планируем завершить предварительный отбор 22 октября 2026 года. Будем благодарны за краткий ответ к этой дате; если это невозможно, пожалуйста, сообщите, когда сможете ответить и принять работу. После ответов и подписания NDA готовы оперативно предоставить полный пакет для оценки стоимости. Краткого ответа на этом этапе вполне достаточно.

С уважением,
Михаил Козин

Dear Mr. Kozin,
Thank you for the detailed clarification. I would be pleased to assist with the U.S. patent applications and assignment matters. My preliminary responses follow your numbering.
1. Scope
Yes. I can prepare and file both U.S. nonprovisional patent applications, review the proposed grouping of the provisional applications, and handle the assignment and USPTO recordation.
I can also assist with preparation and coordination of corresponding PCT applications, subject to confirming the appropriate receiving Office, representation requirements, and applicant eligibility. Russian patent prosecution and related fees would be excluded.
2. Team
I would personally serve as the primary attorney and perform the final substantive review of the specifications, claims, priority claims, and filing documents.
I am a U.S. patent attorney registered with the USPTO, Registration No. 60,225, and have nearly 20 years of patent prosecution experience.
3. PCT Representation
Because you are a Russian citizen residing in the UAE, the appropriate receiving Office and authorized representative must be confirmed before proceeding.
Filing through the International Bureau of WIPO (RO/IB) may be available. However, my U.S. patent registration alone does not necessarily authorize me to act as the formal representative before RO/IB for an applicant whose relevant nationality and residence are outside the United States.
I can prepare and coordinate the technical and application materials and, if necessary, work with an appropriately authorized PCT representative. Any associate's role and fee would be identified and approved before engagement. No PCT filing would be undertaken without separate authorization.
4. Priority
Yes. I can review the official filing receipts, provisional disclosures, inventorship, ownership documents, and proposed priority claims.
Based on the dates provided, December 11, 2026 appears to be the relevant 12-month anniversary for the earliest provisional in NPPA #2, and December 23, 2026 for NPPA #1. These dates remain subject to verification, including applicable deadline rules.
The priority analysis must also determine which subject matter is actually supported by each provisional. Merely identifying several provisional applications in a priority claim does not establish entitlement to each filing date.
The initial review would require the official filing receipts, complete provisional applications and drawings, existing NPPA #1 draft materials, inventor information, and relevant assignment and ownership records.
5. Schedule
I can begin promptly following agreement on the engagement terms and receipt of the necessary materials.
My proposed schedule would prioritize NPPA #2 because of its earlier December 11 priority anniversary.
Subject to the completeness of the materials, I would target an initial NPPA #2 draft within approximately two to three weeks of receiving the technical package, followed by client review and revisions. NPPA #1 could proceed concurrently, with an initial draft or revised version targeted within approximately one to two weeks, depending on the completeness of Ali's existing work.
I would plan to complete both filings ahead of their respective deadlines, allowing time for final approval and filing contingencies. These are preliminary targets, not unconditional commitments before reviewing the materials.
6. Existing Work
Yes. I can take over Ali's unfinished NPPA #1 work and reuse suitable specifications, claims, and drawings after reviewing their completeness, technical accuracy, and suitability for the intended claims.
For NPPA #2, I would evaluate the four identified provisional applications and determine the drafting work needed for a complete nonprovisional application.
My estimate would account for the amount of usable existing material, the number of distinct inventive concepts, claim complexity, and necessary drawings. The agreed fee would include a defined number of ordinary review and revision rounds. Substantial new technical subject matter, major changes in filing strategy, or additional applications would require separate approval.
7. Confidentiality
I am willing to review and sign an appropriate mutual or one-way NDA identifying both Mikhail Kozin and PBK ENGINEERING INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS MANAGEMENT - FZCO as disclosing parties.
I would review the proposed terms before signing and identify any necessary revisions.
8. Insurance and References
I can provide information regarding professional liability coverage and references separately, subject to applicable confidentiality obligations and client consent.
9. Fees
My preliminary professional fee estimates, in U.S. dollars, are:
  • US NPPA #1: $3,500–$5,000, assuming substantial usable existing draft materials.
  • US NPPA #2: $5,000–$7,000, depending on the complexity and completeness of the four provisional disclosures.
  • Assignment review, preparation or revision as necessary, and USPTO recordation: $500–$750.
  • Each corresponding PCT application: $1,000–$1,500 for preparation and coordination using a substantially completed application, subject to confirming representation arrangements.
The indicative combined professional budget for the two U.S. applications and assignment is approximately $9,000–$12,750.
USPTO filing fees, PCT official fees, any additional professional drawings, translations, outside associates, applicable taxes, and platform charges would be separately identified. Entity status and applicable official fees would be verified before filing.
I generally structure larger matters using an initial deposit and milestone payments, with the final balance due before filing. Specific amounts and milestones can be agreed after the scope review.
The estimates exclude office action responses, appeals, additional patent applications, substantive foreign-law advice, Russian patent services, and any separately agreed PCT associate fees.
10. Next Steps
I am willing to conduct an initial, no-charge review of the technical package after execution of an acceptable NDA for the limited purpose of confirming scope, identifying missing materials, and providing a more definite fee proposal.
That preliminary review would not include a comprehensive patentability opinion, formal priority opinion, or detailed ownership analysis. If a substantive preliminary review is necessary, I would first propose its scope and fee for your approval.
No engagement, paid work, or filing would commence without mutually agreed engagement terms and authorization.
I understand your October 22 selection schedule and would welcome the opportunity to assist with these matters.
Best regards,
Michael

Dear Mr. Kozin, 
 
Thank you for the detailed clarification. I would be pleased to assist with the U.S. patent applications and assignment matters. My preliminary responses follow your numbering. 
 
 1. Scope  
 
Yes. I can prepare and file both U.S. nonprovisional patent applications, review the proposed grouping of the provisional applications, and handle the assignment and USPTO recordation. 
 
I can also assist with preparation and coordination of corresponding PCT applications, subject to confirming the appropriate receiving Office, representation requirements, and applicant eligibility. Russian patent prosecution and related fees would be excluded. 
 
 2. Team  
 
I would personally serve as the primary attorney and perform the final substantive review of the specifications, claims, priority claims, and filing documents. 
 
I am a U.S. patent attorney registered with the USPTO, Registration No. 60,225, and have nearly 20 years of patent prosecution experience. 
 
 3. PCT Representation  
 
Because you are a Russian citizen residing in the UAE, the appropriate receiving Office and authorized representative must be confirmed before proceeding. 
 
Filing through the International Bureau of WIPO (RO/IB) may be available. However, my U.S. patent registration alone does not necessarily authorize me to act as the formal representative before RO/IB for an applicant whose relevant nationality and residence
 are outside the United States. 
 
I can prepare and coordinate the technical and application materials and, if necessary, work with an appropriately authorized PCT representative. Any associate's role and fee would be identified and approved before engagement. No PCT filing would be undertaken
 without separate authorization. 
 
 4. Priority  
 
Yes. I can review the official filing receipts, provisional disclosures, inventorship, ownership documents, and proposed priority claims. 
 
Based on the dates provided, December 11, 2026 appears to be the relevant 12-month anniversary for the earliest provisional in NPPA #2, and December 23, 2026 for NPPA #1. These dates remain subject to verification, including applicable deadline rules. 
 
The priority analysis must also determine which subject matter is actually supported by each provisional. Merely identifying several provisional applications in a priority claim does not establish entitlement to each filing date. 
 
The initial review would require the official filing receipts, complete provisional applications and drawings, existing NPPA #1 draft materials, inventor information, and relevant assignment and ownership records. 
 
 5. Schedule  
 
I can begin promptly following agreement on the engagement terms and receipt of the necessary materials. 
 
My proposed schedule would prioritize NPPA #2 because of its earlier December 11 priority anniversary. 
 
Subject to the completeness of the materials, I would target an initial NPPA #2 draft within approximately two to three weeks of receiving the technical package, followed by client review and revisions. NPPA #1 could proceed concurrently, with an initial draft
 or revised version targeted within approximately one to two weeks, depending on the completeness of Ali's existing work. 
 
I would plan to complete both filings ahead of their respective deadlines, allowing time for final approval and filing contingencies. These are preliminary targets, not unconditional commitments before reviewing the materials. 
 
 6. Existing Work  
 
Yes. I can take over Ali's unfinished NPPA #1 work and reuse suitable specifications, claims, and drawings after reviewing their completeness, technical accuracy, and suitability for the intended claims. 
 
For NPPA #2, I would evaluate the four identified provisional applications and determine the drafting work needed for a complete nonprovisional application. 
 
My estimate would account for the amount of usable existing material, the number of distinct inventive concepts, claim complexity, and necessary drawings. The agreed fee would include a defined number of ordinary review and revision rounds. Substantial new
 technical subject matter, major changes in filing strategy, or additional applications would require separate approval. 
 
 7. Confidentiality  
 
I am willing to review and sign an appropriate mutual or one-way NDA identifying both Mikhail Kozin and PBK ENGINEERING INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS MANAGEMENT - FZCO as disclosing parties. 
 
I would review the proposed terms before signing and identify any necessary revisions. 
 
 8. Insurance and References  
 
I can provide information regarding professional liability coverage and references separately, subject to applicable confidentiality obligations and client consent. 
 
 9. Fees  
 
My preliminary professional fee estimates, in U.S. dollars, are: 
 
 
 
US NPPA #1: $3,500–$5,000, assuming substantial usable existing draft materials. 
  
 
US NPPA #2: $5,000–$7,000, depending on the complexity and completeness of the four provisional disclosures. 
  
 
Assignment review, preparation or revision as necessary, and USPTO recordation: $500–$750. 
  
 
Each corresponding PCT application: $1,000–$1,500 for preparation and coordination using a substantially completed application, subject to confirming representation arrangements. 
  
 
The indicative combined professional budget for the two U.S. applications and assignment is approximately $9,000–$12,750. 
 
USPTO filing fees, PCT official fees, any additional professional drawings, translations, outside associates, applicable taxes, and platform charges would be separately identified. Entity status and applicable official fees would be verified before filing. 
 
I generally structure larger matters using an initial deposit and milestone payments, with the final balance due before filing. Specific amounts and milestones can be agreed after the scope review. 
 
The estimates exclude office action responses, appeals, additional patent applications, substantive foreign-law advice, Russian patent services, and any separately agreed PCT associate fees. 
 
 10. Next Steps  
 
I am willing to conduct an initial, no-charge review of the technical package after execution of an acceptable NDA for the limited purpose of confirming scope, identifying missing materials, and providing a more definite fee proposal. 
 
That preliminary review would not include a comprehensive patentability opinion, formal priority opinion, or detailed ownership analysis. If a substantive preliminary review is necessary, I would first propose its scope and fee for your approval. 
 
No engagement, paid work, or filing would commence without mutually agreed engagement terms and authorization. 
 
I understand your October 22 selection schedule and would welcome the opportunity to assist with these matters. 
 
Best regards, 
 
Michael

Subject: Re: U.S. Patent Portfolio — NPPA #1, NPPA #2 and PCT Coordination

Dear Mr. Kozin,

Thank you for your detailed follow-up and for considering IdeaParlor Law for your U.S. patent portfolio.

After further consideration of the expanded scope, international coordination requirements, and approaching priority deadlines, I have concluded that I am not in a position to accept this engagement.

Given the number of applications involved, the ownership and priority issues requiring verification, and the potential need for coordinated U.S. and PCT filings, I believe your interests would be better served by a patent firm with the resources and availability to manage the complete project within the required timeframe.

Accordingly, I will not be proceeding with the proposed confidentiality agreement or further scope assessment.

For clarity, no attorney-client engagement has been established, and IdeaParlor Legal P.C. has not undertaken responsibility for reviewing, monitoring, or meeting any patent filing or priority deadlines.

You have identified potential deadlines of December 11 and December 23, 2026, which remain subject to verification. I strongly recommend engaging qualified patent counsel promptly to independently confirm all applicable deadlines, priority requirements, and filing options.

I appreciate your consideration and wish you success in protecting and developing your patent portfolio.

Best regards,

Anthony Whittington, JD/MBA

The earliest filing in the NPPA #1 group is PPA #3: 63/947,909, December 23, 2025. Our working control dates are December 11, 2026 for group #2 and December 23, 2026 for group #1; please confirm the applicable deadlines and priority support. I am a Russian citizen residing in Sharjah, UAE and do not speak English; written correspondence that I can translate is preferred.

To avoid repeating earlier discussions, a short confirmation of your previous answer is sufficient where applicable. For the remaining points, please reply briefly using the same numbering.

1. Scope: can you prepare and file US NPPA #1 and NPPA #2 and handle the assignment and USPTO recordation? Which PCT services could you provide, subject to eligibility? Russian patent work is excluded.

2. Team: who will be the primary professional and who will personally perform the final review of the specification, claims, priority and filing papers? Please give their professional status and registration number.

3. PCT representation: can you arrange representation taking account of my Russian citizenship and residence in Sharjah, UAE? Who would be entitled to represent the applicant before the proposed receiving Office, including RO/IB, and on what basis? If an associate is needed, please identify the role and cost or how that cost will be agreed.

4. Priority: can you check the official filing receipts, provisional disclosures and chain of title, and confirm the deadlines and basis for priority claims separately for NPPA #1, NPPA #2 and the corresponding PCT applications? Please identify the documents needed for that review.

5. Schedule: when could you start, deliver first drafts, complete review and file each group? Please account for the earliest date in the NPPA #2 group, including a reasonable time buffer and dependencies on us.

6. Existing work: can you take over Ali’s unfinished NPPA #1 work and reuse suitable text and drawings? For NPPA #2, please assess preparation from PPAs #1, #2, #8 and #9; we are not assuming that a completed NPPA #2 draft exists. What is needed for an estimate and which revisions would be charged separately?

7. Confidentiality: can you sign an NDA with two disclosing parties — Mikhail Kozin personally and PBK ENGINEERING INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS MANAGEMENT - FZCO? Please propose any necessary changes. We intend to release the full technical package after the NDA is agreed and signed; if you cannot sign, please let us know.

8. Insurance and references: do you carry professional liability insurance? If available and with the clients’ consent, one or two references would be appreciated. If these details cannot be provided, a brief indication is sufficient.

9. Fees: please itemize US NPPA #1, US NPPA #2, the assignment and USPTO recordation, and each possible PCT filing as a separate option. Separate professional and official fees, drawings, translations, associates and taxes/platform charges; state currency, deposit, milestones, exclusions and the indicative US budget. Do not include Russian services. If materials are needed, please provide a range and conditions for refinement.

10. Next steps: what engagement terms, documents and actions would be needed to begin? Could the initial scope assessment after the NDA be free of charge? If a paid review is needed, please agree its scope and fee with us first. This inquiry and any provision of materials do not accept an engagement or authorize paid work or filing.

We hope to complete our preliminary selection on October 22, 2026. A brief response by then would be greatly appreciated. If that is not possible, please let us know when you could reply and take on the work. After your responses and signature of the agreed NDA, we are ready to provide the full package promptly for a fee assessment. A short response at this stage is entirely sufficient.

Kind regards,
Mikhail Kozin
